input.strategy_title: Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview and adoption is strong, but enterprise
customers will not build production GenAI applications on a TP component.
Graduating to GA requires API stability commitments, a production support
posture, and closing the quality gaps that TP status currently excuses. The
full inventory of those gaps is not yet known — TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets, and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. |
| HLR-3 | P0 | Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. |
| HLR-5 | P1 | The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- TrustyAI
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- New Llama Stack feature development beyond GA-bar quality work
- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

## Open Questions

1. The GA scope itself depends on HLR-1's assessment — until it lands, the
   size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

# Llama Stack GA-readiness assessment and definitive GA scope

## Description

This investigation resolves the strategy's central unknown: the full inventory
of gaps between Llama Stack's current Tech Preview quality and the General
Availability bar. It aggregates the TP feedback scattered across support
tickets, assesses each of the four GA-bar dimensions named by the strategy
(API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), and produces the
definitive GA scope that all downstream Llama Stack hardening and support work
is planned against.

## Scope

- Systematically collect and categorize Tech Preview feedback from support
  tickets and other feedback channels.
- Assess the current Llama Stack distribution against the GA bar on each
  dimension: API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling.
- Produce a severity-ranked gap inventory; for each gap record the current TP
  state, the GA-bar target, and the engineering estimate to close it.
- Produce the definitive GA scope document: which gaps are in scope for GA,
  which are deferred, and the resulting size of the stability and hardening
  work (the strategy currently holds this only as an estimate).
- Route the scope document through stakeholder review and ratification so the
  GA bar and deferrals are agreed, not assumed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A gap inventory exists covering all four assessed dimensions (API
  stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), where each gap
  states the current TP behavior, the GA-bar target, and a severity rating.
- The inventory is traceable to the underlying support-ticket feedback and
  any other cited evidence — every feedback theme in the collected set is
  either reflected in a gap or explicitly dispositioned.
- A definitive GA scope document is produced that enumerates in-scope and
  deferred gaps with engineering estimates for the in-scope items.
- The GA scope document is reviewed and accepted by the strategy
  stakeholders, closing the strategy's open question on GA scope size.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current
  TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error
  handling), producing the definitive GA scope — this epic is that
  assessment.

# Llama Stack GA hardening: API stability, deprecation policy, tested upgrade path, and assessed gap closure

## Description

This epic delivers the published API stability guarantee for Llama Stack as a
GA component: versioned APIs, a documented deprecation policy, and a tested
upgrade path from the last two Tech Preview releases, plus closure of the
code-level GA-bar gaps (including error handling and scale limits) that the
GA-readiness assessment places in scope.

## Scope

- Introduce API versioning on the published API surface of the Llama Stack
  distribution (OpenAI-compatible REST APIs and the distribution's CRD
  surface).
- Define and apply a deprecation policy governing how APIs may change after
  GA, covering the existing TP-era API surface.
- Build and test the upgrade path from each of the last two Tech Preview
  releases to the GA release.
- Close the API-stability, error-handling, and scale-limit gaps that the
  GA-readiness assessment placed in the definitive GA scope, per that
  assessment's severity ranking.
- Keep the hardening within GA-bar quality work; new Llama Stack feature
  development beyond the GA bar is out of scope per the strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published API surface is versioned, and the versioning is applied
  consistently across the documented API surface.
- A deprecation policy is documented and applied to the existing API surface,
  stating how breaking changes are handled for GA consumers.
- An upgrade path from each of the last two Tech Preview releases is tested,
  with passing test evidence for each.
- Every gap the GA-readiness assessment placed in GA scope for API stability,
  error handling, and scale limits is closed in code, or its deferral is
  recorded in the ratified GA scope with rationale.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Published API surface carries a stability guarantee —
  versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last
  two TP releases.
- HLR-1 (P0, partial): implements the code-level gap closure defined by the
  definitive GA scope produced by the readiness assessment.

## Risks / Notes

- Scope is an estimate until the GA-readiness assessment lands; this epic is
  gated on that assessment and its scope is rewritten to the assessed gap
  inventory. If the assessment implies more than roughly two sprints of
  engineering work, split into per-dimension hardening epics (API stability /
  error handling / scale limits) along the assessed gap boundaries.

# Llama Stack production support posture: SLO targets, backport policy, supported configuration matrix

## Description

This epic puts the production support posture in place for Llama Stack as a
GA component: documented SLO targets, a backport policy, and a published
supported configuration matrix. These are the support-process artifacts that
GA status commits the organization to, informed by the scale limits and
quality findings of the GA-readiness assessment.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the GA Llama Stack distribution
  (service-level objectives for the supported surfaces), baselined against
  the quality findings of the GA-readiness assessment.
- Define and document a backport policy covering which releases receive
  fixes and for how long.
- Publish a supported configuration matrix enumerating the configurations
  (providers, deployment sizes, scale limits) validated as supported at GA,
  reflecting the assessed scale limits.
- Route the support posture artifacts through support/product stakeholder
  acceptance so the commitments are ratified, not drafted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documented SLO targets exist for the GA distribution, stating measurable
  targets for the supported surfaces.
- A backport policy is documented, covering the supported release cadence and
  fix backport rules.
- A supported configuration matrix is published, covering the configurations
  validated as supported and reflecting the assessed scale limits.
- The support posture artifacts are accepted by the owning support and
  product stakeholders.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0): Production support posture is in place — documented SLO
  targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix.

## Risks / Notes

- The supported configuration matrix and SLO baselines depend on the
  scale-limit and quality findings of the GA-readiness assessment; this epic
  is gated on that assessment so the posture documents the assessed reality
  rather than a speculative one.

# TrustyAI guardrails as a supported, documented integration for GA distributions

## Description

This epic promotes safety guardrails via TrustyAI from an experimental flag
to a supported integration for GA Llama Stack distributions. The integration
becomes a GA-qualified capability: installed and configured through
supported mechanisms and covered by test evidence. The documentation of the
integration (installation, configuration, support scope, usage) is a
separate content deliverable authored after this work through the Red Hat
docs content process.

## Scope

- Bring the TrustyAI guardrails integration to supported (non-experimental)
  status for GA Llama Stack distributions: remove the experimental/opt-in
  gating for the supported path and make the integration robust enough for
  the production support posture.
- Add end-to-end validation and test coverage for the guardrails integration.
  The validation baseline is the currently shipped Llama Stack distribution
  build (the latest Tech Preview release configuration, deployed via a
  LlamaStackDistribution instance with current shipped defaults) — fixed at
  the current distribution so validation does not wait on the parallel GA
  hardening work. Re-validation of the integration against the GA-hardened
  distribution is deliberately not part of this epic; it is performed and
  recorded at the technical review of the integration documentation
  deliverable, before that documentation is published.
- The integration documentation (installation, configuration, support scope,
  usage) is authored as a separate content deliverable owned by the TrustyAI
  team, published through the Red Hat docs content process and blocked on
  this epic's code work per the docs-last rule — it is not authored here.
- Coordinate the Llama Stack distribution-side wiring with the owning GenAI
  team; if that wiring proves substantial, raise a companion epic rather
  than expanding across the team boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

- TrustyAI guardrails function through the supported path on the named
  validation baseline — the currently shipped Llama Stack distribution build
  (latest Tech Preview release configuration) — with no experimental/TP
  opt-in flag required for the supported configuration.
- End-to-end test evidence exists showing guardrails enforcing via TrustyAI
  on that validation baseline (the currently shipped Llama Stack
  distribution build), testable without waiting for the GA-hardened
  distribution.
- The TrustyAI team lead (integration owner) records sign-off that the
  guardrails integration is within the production support posture for GA
  distributions, as an approval comment on the end-to-end test evidence that
  names the tested supported configuration.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. This epic
  delivers the supported integration and its test evidence; the
  documentation deliverable is carried by the TrustyAI integration
  documentation work that follows this epic.

# Dashboard Llama Stack management default-on for entitled clusters

## Description

This epic enables Llama Stack management in the Dashboard by default for
entitled clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate. Entitled users see
Llama Stack management surfaces without any opt-in action; clusters without
entitlement are unaffected.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard enablement logic so Llama Stack management is
  default-on for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate).
- Preserve current behavior for clusters without the entitlement — no broken
  or partially rendered surfaces.
- Keep the enablement reversible through the Dashboard's existing
  per-component feature-flag/configuration mechanism so the default can be
  reverted without code rollback.
- Update any captions, labels, or references that fall out of the default-on
  change (e.g., removal of Tech Preview disclaimers on the management
  surfaces) — incidental touch-ups, no new content authored here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster, Llama Stack management surfaces are available in
  the Dashboard by default, with no opt-in action required.
- On a cluster without entitlement, the Dashboard behaves as before — Llama
  Stack management is not shown broken or partially rendered.
- The default-on state is reversible via Dashboard configuration (feature
  flag) without code rollback, verified by test.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P1): The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for
  entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate).

# Llama Stack GA documentation uplift and TP migration notes

## Description

This epic uplifts Llama Stack documentation to GA standards and authors the
migration notes that move existing Tech Preview users to the GA release. It
runs through the Red Hat docs content process and describes the GA
deliverable as actually built: the stability guarantee, the support posture,
and the default-on management experience.

## Scope

Content outline (authored through the Red Hat docs content process):

- GA overview and support statements for Llama Stack: maturity, support
  posture summary, and links to the supported configuration matrix and SLO
  documentation.
- Installation and configuration documentation aligned to the supported
  configuration matrix.
- API usage documentation reflecting the versioned API surface and the
  deprecation policy.
- Migration notes from Tech Preview to GA, covering the upgrade path from
  the last two TP releases and the behavior changes (including Dashboard
  default-on management and the supported TrustyAI guardrails integration).
- Removal of Tech Preview disclaimers and experimental caveats from topics
  covering GA-supported surfaces.

Out of scope: the TrustyAI guardrails integration documentation itself
(installation, configuration, support scope, usage), which the TrustyAI team
authors as its own documentation deliverable through the same Red Hat docs
content process.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Llama Stack documentation topics covering GA-supported surfaces carry no
  Tech Preview disclaimers and meet GA documentation standards.
- Migration notes from Tech Preview (from each of the last two TP releases)
  are published and cover the upgrade path and behavior changes.
- All new and revised content is technically reviewed against the
  implemented GA behavior (reviewed against the actual implementation, not
  the plan).
- Documentation is published through the Red Hat docs content process.

## HLR Traceability

## Description

This epic authors and publishes the documentation for the supported TrustyAI
guardrails integration with Llama Stack — installation, configuration,
support scope, and usage — through the Red Hat docs content process as part
of the GA documentation set. It delivers the "documented" half of the
supported, documented integration; the code, the removal of the experimental
gating, and the test evidence are delivered by the TrustyAI guardrails
integration work this documentation follows.

## Scope

- Installation and configuration documentation for TrustyAI guardrails on GA
  Llama Stack distributions, using the supported (non-experimental)
  mechanisms.
- Support-scope statements for the integration, aligned with the Llama Stack
  production support posture (SLO targets and the supported configuration
  matrix).
- Usage documentation covering enabling and configuring guardrails via
  TrustyAI on a LlamaStackDistribution, including the default-on Dashboard
  management path where it touches the integration.
- Publication through the Red Hat docs content process — the same route as
  the general GA documentation uplift — not in-repo engineering notes only.

  not wait on the GA hardening; this epic is where the re-check against the

  scope, and usage of TrustyAI guardrails with Llama Stack is published
  through the Red Hat docs content process, with no experimental disclaimers

  implemented integration (the actual code and test evidence, not the plan).

  Llama Stack distribution before publication: end-to-end guardrails
  enforcement is re-checked on the GA distribution build and the results are
  recorded alongside the technical review, closing the gap left by the
  integration work's Tech Preview-baseline validation.
- Support-scope statements in the integration documentation match the
  published Llama Stack support posture (SLO targets and the supported
  configuration matrix).

  a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA
  distributions — this epic delivers the documentation half; the supported
  integration and its test evidence are delivered by the TrustyAI guardrails
  integration work.
